Method_Options: (A) Thiessen/Voronoi polygons; (B) IDW (Inverse Distance Weighting); (C) Kriging (Ordinary or Universal); (D) Approved gridded product (CHIRPS / ERA5 / TAMSAT)
Recommended_Method: Gridded product (CHIRPS) preferred if station count < 5 per state; IDW or Kriging if >= 5 stations per state with good spatial distribution
Method_Rationale: Station density in Nigeria is low and uneven. CHIRPS (Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data) provides 0.05-degree (~5km) daily rainfall estimates blending satellite and station data — widely validated for West Africa. Recommended as primary product where station-only interpolation is unreliable. Station-based IDW or Kriging used where station coverage is sufficient for cross-validation.
Minimum_Stations_Required: 5 active stations with good spatial distribution per interpolation domain
Cross_Validation_Method: Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) where >= 5 stations; satellite-station comparison where gridded product used
Notes: CHIRPS source: https://www.chc.ucsb.edu/data/chirps. ERA5 alternative: https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu. Method MUST be documented and consistent across all years in the baseline. If method changes between updates a new version must be created.

Method_Options: (A) Thiessen/Voronoi polygons; (B) IDW; (C) Kriging; (D) Lapse-rate adjusted IDW (elevation correction); (E) Approved gridded product (ERA5 / CRU)
Recommended_Method: Lapse-rate adjusted IDW if >= 4 stations; ERA5 gridded product if stations insufficient
Method_Rationale: Temperature has strong elevation dependency (lapse rate ~6.5°C/1000m). Lapse-rate correction using G09 DEM is recommended where station coverage permits. ERA5 provides 0.25-degree reanalysis temperature — lower resolution than CHIRPS but reliable for Nigeria. Station-only IDW without elevation correction is not recommended for study area given varied terrain in Cross River/Enugu/Kogi highlands.
Minimum_Stations_Required: 4 active stations with elevation metadata for lapse-rate method
Cross_Validation_Method: LOOCV where stations sufficient; ERA5 comparison
Notes: ERA5 source: https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu. CRU TS alternative: https://crudata.uea.ac.uk/cru/data/hrg. Lapse rate: use standard environmental lapse rate of 6.5°C/1000m unless local measured lapse rate available. Document which lapse rate used.

Method_Options: Annual means vs seasonal means vs monthly means vs daily
Recommended_Method: Annual and seasonal means for baseline; monthly means for trend analysis
Method_Rationale: Annual and seasonal (wet/dry season) means provide the most stable baseline for risk analysis. Monthly means used for trend detection. Daily interpolated surfaces not required for baseline — too uncertain with available station density.
Notes: Nigeria wet season: approximately April-October in south; May-September in north. Dry season: November-March (south); October-April (north). Seasonal boundaries should be defined before baseline computation.

Method_Options: Match DEM (90m or 30m); 0.05 degree (CHIRPS native); 0.25 degree (ERA5 native); 1km resampled
Recommended_Method: 0.05 degree (~5km) for rainfall (CHIRPS native); 0.25 degree (~25km) for temperature (ERA5 native) OR resampled to 0.05 degree
Method_Rationale: Outputting at native gridded product resolution avoids false precision. For station-based interpolation match DEM resolution. Resolution mismatch between G22/G23 and G09 terrain layers must be documented in hazard model (G24).
Notes: Resolution must be fixed before G22/G23 are computed and documented in metadata
